projects.name: Frontier AI Valuation Lab
projects.summary: A financing workspace that connects capital objectives, ownership scenarios and a reviewable decision, with a seeded Monte Carlo range for modeled value.
projects.scenario: Compare hypothetical financing plans, change a retained-ownership objective and inspect where the ranking changes. Then open the Monte Carlo panel: ranges on the growth path, terminal margin, discount rate and terminal growth, joined by a Gaussian copula, give P5 to P95 values and a one-way P10 to P90 tornado.
projects.inspect: Follow the shared calculation engine and Node API, then compare with the independent Python references. The simulate action reuses the unchanged DCF engine for every draw, and the same request returns byte-identical JSON in the browser and the API.
projects.limits: Independent research with illustrative assumptions; company names imply no affiliation or endorsement. Simulated percentiles describe the entered ranges, not a forecast or a probability that a company is worth any amount.
projects.command:
npm test
python3 -B scripts/check_uncertainty_reference.py --output /tmp/uncertainty-reference.json
npm start

projects.name: crossbook
projects.summary: A deterministic order-matching engine with opening and closing call auctions, crash recovery, market data and multi-instrument sharding, checked against a second implementation.
projects.scenario: Run the auction demo: an opening call collects orders without trading, prints the indicative uncross after each one, rejects an immediate-or-cancel order and uncrosses 13 lots at 101, market orders first. Then run one million synthetic orders in the playground and compare the event digest with the native build.
projects.inspect: Follow the one-pass clearing-price search over cached level totals, then the brute-force uncross that tries every candidate price. They agree on 20,000 seeded books on which each of the five price rules decides at least 126 times, and every uncross passes seven allocation invariants.
projects.limits: Books kept in memory in one process, on synthetic order flow. No network gateway, journals written without fsync, and no connection to any market. The clearing price is always one of the orders’ limits, there are no volatility interruptions, and the feed publishes no indicative price.
projects.command:
cargo run --release -p crossbook-cli -- demo
cargo run --release -p crossbook-cli -- auction
cargo run --release -p crossbook-cli -- verify --orders 1000000

projects.name: LineageGuard Studio
projects.summary: Typed schema-change review workflows with evidence from fixtures, DataHub or a dbt manifest, policy checks and recovery.
projects.scenario: Review a column rename against a real dbt manifest from a synthetic project: renaming fct_mrr.mrr_usd lists five downstream models, two exposures with owners and 12 dbt tests, and stays at needs-evidence because a manifest cannot show usage or column lineage. The Studio runs the same file as its dbt manifest scenario.
projects.inspect: Follow the offline manifest adapter: version refusal, agreement between parent_map, child_map and depends_on, cycle checks and owner precedence. A seeded property test compares lineage with an independent walk of depends_on, and 16 of the 105 labelled benchmark cases run on the manifest.
projects.limits: Synthetic demonstration; optional DataHub integration is read-only. The dbt adapter reads manifest schema v12 and catalog v1 only, and its lineage is model-level, so manifest evidence can block a change or ask for more but never clear one. Saved-export checks establish internal consistency, not source truth, authenticated approval or migration authority.
projects.command:
npm run studio:review -- --dbt-manifest=public/studio/dbt/saas-analytics-warehouse/manifest.json --dbt-catalog=public/studio/dbt/saas-analytics-warehouse/catalog.json --request=examples/dbt/rename-mrr-usd.json --output=./.lineageguard/dbt-review.json
npm run studio:benchmark -- --check
# Use new export paths when repeating; existing outputs are never overwritten.

projects.name: SaaS Analytics Warehouse
projects.summary: A reproducible analytics pipeline for MRR, retention and unit economics, with incremental loads and a type 2 history of subscription state.
projects.scenario: Build the fictional warehouse, then load the same rows day by day with late arrivals and confirm that the incremental build equals a full refresh. Look up any customer’s plan and MRR on a past date in the snapshot, or trace one historical month from the MRR bridge to customer records.
projects.inspect: Follow the 7-day lookback and delete+insert staging models, the business-time snapshot with its four history tests, and the load simulation that compares 24 relations with a full refresh by row hashes. The churn investigation still reconciles exact cents and customer counts before writing reports.
projects.limits: Seeded fictional SaaS data; results describe the fixture, not a real business. Rows more than 7 days late are missed until a full refresh, the marts still rebuild in full, and incremental runs are not faster at this size because the sources are CSV files read in full.
projects.command:
uv sync --locked
make data build MONTHS=24 SCALE=0.25
uv run python -m saasreport.churn --month 2024-12 --output-dir ../tallyloom-churn-2024-12
make incremental-check MONTHS=6 SCALE=0.25 DAILY_DAYS=14

projects.name: Impact Ledger
projects.summary: Participation and spending reporting with a local API, atomic CSV imports and a hash-chained audit log that rebuilds past reports.
projects.scenario: Import sessions and attendance, rebuild the summary as of the entry before the attendance import, undo that import with a compensating batch, then verify the log. The undone import stays in the history.
projects.inspect: Follow the audit log written in the same SQLite transaction as each change. Triggers block edits and deletions, and verify detects edited, deleted or reordered entries and table edits that bypass the log. As-of reports replay the verified log prefix.
projects.limits: Hosted preview is read-only and synthetic; writes require running the local application. The log is tamper-evident, not tamper-proof, and actor labels are self-declared. On a 25,000-entry synthetic ledger an as-of summary took 315 ms against 68 ms from the current tables.
projects.command:
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db init
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db import sessions examples/sessions.csv
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db import attendance examples/attendance.csv
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db summary --as-of-entry 2
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db undo-import B000003
python3 -m impact_ledger --db .local/example.db verify

projects.name: ContrastKit
projects.summary: Color contrast auditing across a web app, library and CLI, with color-vision simulation that includes anomalous trichromacy at any severity.
projects.scenario: Check a green and red pair under deuteranomaly at severity 0.6 and under deuteranopia, then move the severity slider in the Palette Auditor. Or download a failing palette as tokens JSON, audit it with the CLI, apply the suggested fix and confirm that the next download passes.
projects.inspect: Follow the interpolation between Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes’s published 0.1 steps into audits and the CLI’s --cvd option. 810 simulations agree with colorspacious 1.1.2 within 5e-13, and 990 at the published steps agree with DaltonLens 0.1.5 within one 8-bit step.
projects.limits: Color checks support accessibility work; they do not constitute a complete accessibility audit. Simulation approximates an average observer: severity is a model parameter, not a clinical measure, and tritan simulations are the least reliable.
projects.command:
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
npx contrastkit check 2f855a c53030 --cvd deuteranomaly:0.6 --cvd deuteranopia

projects.name: MOTIONX Studio
projects.summary: A motion-led studio website with a separate outreach-validation workflow.
projects.scenario: Explore the responsive studio pages, then inspect how the separate Python workflow validates outreach inputs.
projects.inspect: Follow the frontend structure and architecture notes; review validation boundaries independently of the public website.
projects.limits: Public site and validation tooling are separate. A website preview does not demonstrate outreach delivery or client adoption.
projects.command:
npm ci
npm run dev -- -p 3939

projects.name: RelayBox
projects.summary: A durable signed-webhook inbox with idempotency and fenced worker leases, plus outbound delivery signed per the Standard Webhooks specification.
projects.scenario: Subscribe the example receiver, publish a message and deliver it: the first attempt gets 503 with Retry-After, and the retry succeeds with the same webhook-id and a new timestamp. The inbound demo still delivers the same signed event twice and shows retry, lease and recovery behavior.
projects.inspect: Follow full-jitter backoff, the dead-letter queue and replay in the dispatcher. Signing matches the specification’s published test vector, and a dispatcher killed mid-request leaves its lease, after which another resends the same message with the same webhook-id.
projects.limits: Local single-host SQLite service; outbound targets are loopback-only unless explicitly allowed. No rate limit or circuit breaker, and signing secrets are stored unencrypted. Diagnostic samples are not throughput or service-level claims.
projects.command:
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/demo.sqlite3 demo
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/demo.sqlite3 serve --demo-secret
# Outbound: start the receiver in one terminal, then deliver from another
python3 examples/receive_webhooks.py --demo-secret --fail-first 1
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/out.sqlite3 subscription add http://127.0.0.1:8788/hook --event-type example.created --demo-secret
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/out.sqlite3 publish example.created examples/payload.json
python3 -m relaybox --db .local/out.sqlite3 deliver --max-deliveries 10 --wait 15

projects.name: TraceBench
projects.summary: Offline evaluation of recorded AI outputs with exact supplied-cost accounting and statistical regression gates.
projects.scenario: Compare two candidates with a 100-case synthetic baseline. The noisy one swaps 5 passing and 5 failing cases; the regressed one breaks 12 and fixes 1. The default any-regression gate fails both, while the exact McNemar gate passes the noisy candidate and fails the regressed one.
projects.inspect: Follow the exact McNemar test, seeded paired bootstrap intervals and minimum detectable effects into the --gate options. On synthetic 100-case suites where 10% of cases flip at random, any-regression failed 99.4% of unchanged suites and McNemar 1.1%.
projects.limits: Evaluates supplied recorded outputs; it does not call a model or measure live model quality. Gates judge pass/fail only and assume independent cases, and a 100-case suite can only detect pass-rate changes of about 0.09.
projects.command:
mkdir -p reports
python3 -m tracebench evaluate --cases fixtures/paired/cases.jsonl --outputs fixtures/paired/baseline.jsonl --pricing fixtures/pricing.json --report reports/paired-baseline.json
python3 -m tracebench evaluate --cases fixtures/paired/cases.jsonl --outputs fixtures/paired/noisy.jsonl --pricing fixtures/pricing.json --baseline reports/paired-baseline.json --gate mcnemar
python3 -m tracebench evaluate --cases fixtures/paired/cases.jsonl --outputs fixtures/paired/regressed.jsonl --pricing fixtures/pricing.json --baseline reports/paired-baseline.json --gate mcnemar --format markdown

projects.name: quantkit
projects.summary: Options pricing, portfolio optimization, backtesting and VaR model validation, checked against independent references.
projects.scenario: Simulate fictional prices, forecast one-day 99% VaR and expected shortfall each day from the previous 250, and backtest the forecasts with the Kupiec and Christoffersen tests, the Basel traffic light and the Acerbi–Székely Z2 test.
projects.inspect: Follow the four rolling forecasters into the exception tests. A dynamic program gives each test’s exact size: at 250 days a correct model fails the nominal 5% Kupiec test 9.5% of the time, and a simulation measures 10.5%. A perturbation test keeps every forecast blind to the return it is scored against.
projects.limits: Educational quantitative software on synthetic data; no investment recommendation or live execution. VaR covers one day and one return series, its likelihood-ratio p-values are asymptotic, and the traffic light is the 1996 table for 250 days of 99% VaR.
projects.command:
uv sync
uv run quantkit simulate --output prices.csv
uv run quantkit var-backtest prices.csv --method ewma --level 0.99

projects.name: powerlift
projects.summary: Experiment statistics with power analysis, multi-arm (A/B/n) tests with Dunnett’s correction, CUPED, sequential monitoring and Bayesian tools.
projects.scenario: Read a seeded synthetic CSV with one control and three variants: the SRM check runs across all four arms, and Dunnett’s test finds only variant D different while holding the family-wise false-win rate at 5%. Plan the sample size for three arms, or compare raw and CUPED-adjusted estimates in the two-arm readout.
projects.inspect: Follow the many-to-one analysis into the max-|t| distribution, where the shared control turns a k-dimensional integral into a two-dimensional one. Results agree with scipy.stats.dunnett, and simulated family-wise error under the global null is 5.1% for Dunnett against 13.5% unadjusted with three variants.
projects.limits: Statistical results depend on study design and data assumptions; a significant result alone is not a business decision. Multi-arm comparisons are many-to-one and single-step, and they pool the arms’ variance.
projects.command:
uv sync
uv run python examples/multi_arm_simulation.py --csv arms.csv
uv run powerlift analyze --csv arms.csv --group-col arm --value-col revenue_usd --control-label A --treatment-label B --treatment-label C --treatment-label D

projects.name: ledgerline
projects.summary: A double-entry ledger API with immutable balanced entries, idempotent writes and holds (two-phase transfers) that report ledger, held and available balances.
projects.scenario: In the API walkthrough, authorize a hold, confirm that the ledger balance is unchanged while the available balance falls, capture part of it, void another and let one expire. The disposable local HTTP wallet still deposits, transfers, retries with the same key, rejects an overdraft, reverses and reconciles.
projects.inspect: Follow how holds and postings draw on one available balance through the account version check: 40 concurrent 30-cent holds against 1,000 cents give exactly 33, and ten racing captures and voids of one hold produce one winner. A Hypothesis state machine checks holds, captures, voids and expiry against a model.
projects.limits: Engineering demonstration; it is not a bank, payment processor or accounting system certification. A hold allows one capture, expiry is computed when read, and the destination does not see pending credits.
projects.command:
uv sync
uv run python examples/wallet_demo.py
uv run pytest tests/test_holds_concurrency.py -v

projects.name: searchlite
projects.summary: A full-text search engine with compressed postings, MaxScore top-k pruning, explainable ranking and retrieval evaluation.
projects.scenario: Compare two saved local indexes with your own relevance judgments in the browser, inspect query-level regressions and download the native-compatible report. Then run the pruning property tests: on random corpora, queries, filters and limits, the pruned top-k equals scoring every match.
projects.inspect: Follow delta and varint blocks of 128 documents with skip entries and per-block score bounds into MaxScore windows. At 10,000 synthetic documents, median top-10 latency fell from 2.06 to 0.30 ms (glossary) and 8.48 to 0.57 ms (Zipf) with byte-identical rankings. The local-file worker shares validation, ranking and the strict per-query gate with the native command.
projects.limits: Small in-memory library. Pruning gains are smaller at 1,000 documents, one phrase-heavy query is slower, and block-max WAND is not implemented. Files stay in page memory, and exported reports contain query text and document IDs. Synthetic judgments and timing fixtures do not establish general retrieval quality or production latency.
projects.command:
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build
npx vitest run test/engine/pruning.test.ts
searchlite_review_dir=$(mktemp -d)
searchlite_review_dir=$(cd "$searchlite_review_dir" && pwd -P)
node examples/search-docs.js index examples/fixtures/relevance-notes "$searchlite_review_dir/notes.json"
node examples/search-docs.js evaluate "$searchlite_review_dir/notes.json" examples/fixtures/relevance-notes/judgments.json

projects.name: citecheck
projects.summary: Document question answering with retrieved citations, a claim-level support checker and abstention evaluation.
projects.scenario: Index the sample handbook and ask a question whose prepared answer flips a negation: the word-overlap checker rates that sentence supported, while the claim-level checker flags it. Then score both checkers on 77 held-out labelled claims.
projects.inspect: Follow claim splitting, clause alignment and the negation, modality, opposite-word and quantity checks. On the held-out cases the claim-level checker caught 44 of 48 unsupported sentences against 20 of 48 for word overlap, with 2 false flags on 29 supported sentences against 1 (exact McNemar p = 1.5e-06).
projects.limits: Offline fixture responses are hand-written, and one author wrote both the claim cases and the rules, so the held-out figures are optimistic. The checks are rules, not entailment. Live answers require provider configuration and may incur usage charges.
projects.command:
uv sync
uv run citecheck index examples/handbook
uv run citecheck ask "Do I need a doctor's note when I take a sick day?"
uv run citecheck eval-claims

projects.name: ProofCast
projects.summary: Local media generation with provenance records, Ed25519 manifest signatures and a Merkle transparency log.
projects.scenario: Generate a local bundle, then run the tamper demo: it signs and logs the bundle on copies and catches a changed media byte, a changed manifest byte, a different trusted key, a flipped proof bit, an edited tree head and a rewritten log entry.
projects.inspect: Follow the RFC 6962 and RFC 9162 Merkle tree, its inclusion and consistency proofs and the signed tree heads. The proofs match 195 of 196 published transparency-dev/merkle probes; the remaining probe passes placeholder roots and is rejected on purpose.
projects.limits: Local workflow demonstration. A signature proves which key signed, not who holds the key, and a digest does not prove authorship or the truth of media content. The log is one local file without independent witnesses, the private key is stored unencrypted, and the optional B2 upload has not been run against a real bucket.
projects.command:
.venv/bin/python -m proofcast.cli --title "Synthetic demo" --script "A local verification example."
.venv/bin/python examples/tamper_demo.py output/YOUR-RUN-ID-manifest.json

projects.name: Luma Keys
projects.summary: Offline piano practice with score views, planned fingering and graded sight reading.
projects.scenario: Build a disposable browser session, generate an exercise, play clean and flawed timed runs, then inspect saved progress and repeat the exact seed.
projects.inspect: Run five sight-reading stories and inspect screenshots, failure receipts, owned-server cleanup and Web Audio practice grading without optional engines.
projects.limits: Browser QA uses synthetic exercises with 3-D hands off on macOS/Linux. Physical input, native packaging and optional engines need separate verification.

npm ci --ignore-scripts
npx playwright install chromium --only-shell
npm test
npm run qa:browser -- --output-dir .qa-runs/reviewer-exercise

projects.name: Blast Radius Daily
projects.summary: A one-minute Reddit puzzle about downstream effects of schema changes, playable with a pointer or a keyboard.
projects.scenario: Pick a UTC incident day, place two circuit breakers with the mouse or with Tab, the arrow keys and Space, trace the real cascade, compare the computed result, move one synthetic vote, then delete and replay.
projects.inspect: Open the playable offline build or produce its single HTML yourself. Follow the shared engine, the hidden accessible mirror of the board with its live announcements, the exact source/build lock and the offline Chromium journeys, three of which never touch the mouse.
projects.limits: Desktop/landscape demo; fictional community data lives in tab memory and reload resets it. Comments are unavailable. Keyboard and screen-reader support is checked with Playwright and axe-core in Chromium, not with a physical screen reader or inside Reddit’s apps. Live Reddit/Redis behavior and portrait layout require separate verification.
projects.command:
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build:demo
# Open dist-demo/blast-radius-demo.html from disk
npx playwright install chromium --only-shell
npm run test:demo

projects.name: Agentic Trading Research
projects.summary: An offline research architecture with a runnable fail-closed review gate and backtest-overfitting diagnostics.
projects.scenario: Run the overfitting demo: the best of 100 no-skill synthetic strategies has a naive PSR of 0.9989, yet the deflated Sharpe ratio, PBO, White’s Reality Check and Hansen’s SPA all flag it, while a strategy with injected skill passes all four. Then run the six fail-closed gate scenarios.
projects.inspect: Follow the standard-library PSR and DSR, CSCV, stationary bootstrap and SPA code. Tests check the published DSR example, compare PBO with a brute-force version, run null simulations and show that each of eight deliberate mutations fails a test.
projects.limits: Research-review-only demonstration with synthetic fixtures; no automated orders, brokerage connection or trading advice. The diagnostics use independent Student-t returns without costs, and none of them shows that a strategy is profitable.
projects.command:
python3 -B examples/overfitting_demo.py
python3 -B examples/fail_closed_gate.py --all
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s examples -p "test_*.py" -v

projects.name: JUST-QR
projects.summary: A minimal browser QR generator with its own ISO/IEC 18004 encoder and image export.
projects.scenario: Generate and export a QR code at the default error-correction level H, try an invalid or oversized destination, recover with a valid URL, lower the level to fit a longer one and compare the clipboard and download images.
projects.inspect: Follow qr.js through Reed-Solomon coding with block interleaving, format and version information and mask selection by the four penalty rules. Tests match the ISO and zxing vectors, decode random symbols across 30+ versions with jsQR, and compare 120 symbols module for module with qrcodejs.
projects.limits: Browser utility; a QR code encodes input and does not validate whether the destination is trustworthy. One segment per code, with no ECI, Kanji, Micro QR or structured append. The page loads no third-party script but still requests two Google Fonts, and it must be served over HTTP.
projects.command:
python3 -m http.server 8000
npm ci
npx playwright install chromium --only-shell
npm test
